title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Amendment (Strategic Assets) Bill 2015
short_title: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Amendment (Strategic Assets) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would keep certain Australian assets in the hands of the Australian people.
It would stop foreign buyers from gaining a 10% or larger stake in land, water or other assets the government deems strategically important, with a new board deciding what qualifies.
A foreign buyer could still acquire up to a 45% interest if both houses of Parliament approve it by a two-thirds majority vote.
changes: Creates the Foreign Ownership Assessment Board to decide which assets are strategically important.
Bans foreign persons from acquiring a 10% or greater interest in assets of strategic economic or defensive importance.
Allows a 45% interest in such assets if both chambers of Parliament pass a resolution with a two-thirds majority.
Lets decisions by the board be appealed to a tribunal, and tribunal decisions to a court.
Requires the board to be funded from normal budget supply.
summary.affected: Foreign persons and entities seeking to buy Australian land, water or other assets.
